sections.name: Hero Section
sections.title: Car Accident Injury Symptoms to Watch For

paras.t: Some crash injuries show up right away. A lot of them don't. Here's what to watch for in the days after a wreck, and when to get checked.

sections.name: Intro Section
sections.title: Feeling fine doesn't mean you're fine

paras.t: Adrenaline covers a lot in the first day or two. Neck and back injuries often surface two to four days after a crash, sometimes longer. By then the insurance adjuster may have already called to ask how you're feeling.
Getting checked early tells you whether something's wrong and puts it on record from the start.

cards.title: Neck pain or stiffness
cards.text: Trouble turning your head, a stiff neck the next morning, or pain that runs into your shoulders. These are the classic signs of whiplash.

cards.title: Back pain
cards.text: Anything from a sore, tight lower back to pain that runs into the buttock or down a leg, which can mean a nerve is involved.

cards.title: Numbness or tingling
cards.text: In your hands, arms, legs, or feet. Even without much pain, this can point to a pinched nerve or a disc injury.

cards.title: Headaches
cards.text: Headaches that start after a crash can come from the neck. They can also come from a concussion, which needs a medical doctor first (see below).

cards.title: Shoulder pain
cards.text: Often comes from the neck after a crash, especially if you were wearing a seatbelt across that shoulder.

paras.t: Go to an emergency room, not a chiropractor, if you have:
These can be signs of a fracture, internal injury, or concussion. Get those ruled out first. We're here once they are.

cards.title: Pain in your ribs, chest, or belly, or trouble taking a full breath
A headache with confusion, dizziness, vomiting, or trouble remembering the crash
Numbness or weakness that's spreading or getting worse
Loss of bladder or bowel control

sections.name: Exam Section
sections.title: What Dr. Morgan checks after a crash

paras.t: With a crash patient, Dr. Morgan is looking for more than a stiff neck. He checks how your neck moves in every direction, where it hurts and where it doesn't, and whether there's any numbness, tingling, or headaches that point to a nerve being involved. He also asks about the crash itself, because the direction of the hit tells him where to look.

On the X-ray, a healthy neck has a gentle curve. After a crash, that curve often straightens out, the head shifts forward, and the joints stop moving together the way they should. Those findings turn "my neck is sore" into a documented injury.

callouts.title: Most car accident patients also get an MRI referral.
callouts.text: Disc injuries are more likely after a crash, so Dr. Morgan refers most crash patients for one.

faqs.q: How long after a car accident can symptoms show up?
faqs.a: Often two to four days, sometimes longer. That's why it's worth getting checked even if you feel fine.

faqs.q: Is it normal to feel worse a few days after the crash?
faqs.a: It's common. Stiffness and pain often peak a few days later as the adrenaline wears off and inflammation sets in. Get checked if it's getting worse.
In most cases, no. PIP, a letter of protection, or a third-party claim usually covers it. We'll confirm which applies to you before treatment starts.

faqs.q: How soon can I be seen?
faqs.a: Often the same day. Call and tell us you were in an accident.
